episodes.195881: An anomalously strong upper low from the west over AZ resulted in shower activity across western NM on October 18th resulting in some high wind gusts across parts of western and central NM. As the upper low remained nearly stationary over AZ heading into October 19th, it helped pull up abundant moisture from the Gulf of Mexico into eastern NM producing widespread strong to severe storms over portions of the eastern plains, mainly south of I-25. Bands of showers and thunderstorms first produced very heavy rainfall over a long twelve to eighteen hour period totaling 2 to 6 inches over the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar. Thankfully there were only reports of nuisance flooding in this area on October 19th. Storms developing along the highlands late on the afternoon and evening of the 19th organized into a line over eastern portions of Lincoln County and western portions of Chaves County. This line of storms shifted eastward over the Pecos River Valley during the evening of the 19th producing historically high rainfall. The as of this date all-time record daily maximum rainfall amount at Roswell of 5.78 inches was recorded, with numerous other mesonet and public weather stations recording 4 to 9 inches in Roswell. Fatal flash flooding resulted in Roswell with reports of flooding inundating homes forcing people to their attics and rooftops, and vehicles being stranded and washed away. The Chaves County Sheriff recorded a video of himself being stranded on his vehicle alongside two other individuals in flood waters after trying to respond to an incident. River flooding was observed along the Rio Felix and Pecos River in Chaves County. This river flooding washed out NM Highway 2 in Hagerman along the Rio Felix. The Pecos River reached 20.34 feet at the Lake Arthur gage, which was minor stage before receding. The Chaves County Emergency Manager reported that flooding did not recede until Monday morning on October 22nd in Roswell. Another round of severe storms with damaging wind gusts and large hail impacted northeast NM during the evening and early overnight hours of October 20th before the storm system exited the state.||Key Impacts: Flash flooding, hail, thunderstorm wind gusts.

events.narrative: Quarter size hail was reported at the Burnt Well Guest Ranch from a severe thunderstorm.

U.S. Highway 285 washed out at mile marker 137 and mile marker 151 due to heavy rainfall from thunderstorms. Additionally, NMDOT closed U.S. Highway 285 from mile marker 135 to 138 due to flash flooding. Flash flooding resulted in vehicles being stuck in several inches of water and multiple areas of the highway becoming impassable. An accident also occurred on the highway about 14 miles north of Roswell due to hydroplaning.
Thunderstorms produced a peak wind gust of 66 mph at the Roswell Air Center.

Historically bad flash flooding across Roswell, reported by numerous emergency officials and the public. Thunderstorms training over Roswell dumped an all-time one-day rainfall record of 5.78 at the Roswell Airport with numerous other public weather stations across town ranging from 4 to 9 inches. Major flooding was reported across the city and nearby low-lying areas south and west of town. Numerous vehicles were submerged in over 4 feet of water while several more were swept away. The Roswell Daily Record reported that as many as 500 rescues were carried out over the weekend during and after the flooding. Estimates have as many as 400 homes and 200 businesses facing significant damage. The Roswell Convention Center was hosting a UFO festival when flood waters up to 5 feet entered the building. Attendees were being rescued from the rooftop. Roswell's Spring River Zoo also suffered extensive damage including the loss of one donkey. Flood damage was also sustained to Roswell's Landfill and Wastewater Treatment Plant. All roads entering the city were closed by State Police. The city lost 4 fire trucks and 7 police patrol cars with numerous city facilities damaged. There is one confirmed direct fatality from drowning and one indirect fatality from a heart attack reported and there may have been more as many vehicles were swept away along the Spring River drainage.
Two feet of water reported at the Burnt Well Guest Ranch where roadways near the ranch were flooded.

The NM Department of Transportation reported river flooding along the Rio Felix south of Roswell overtopping and damaging the U.S. Highway 285 bridge, and overtopping  the NM State Highway 2 bridge just north of Hagerman closing both bridges. Flooding from heavy rains and poor drainage also extended over much of Dexter just north of Hagerman. Damage is an estimate. A Flood Warning was issued and repeatedly extended until local reports of the water receding came from local Emergency Management.

Historically bad flash flooding across Roswell from storms dropping 4 to 9 inches across town, including an all-time one-day precipitation record of 5.78 at the Roswell airport caused major damage. This flooding was reported to have persisted through Monday October 21st. Damage and fatality information are recorded in the preceding flash flood entry.

A forecasted rise in the Pecos River at the ACME gauge just north of U.S. Highway 70 was to 13.2 feet, or to minor flood stage. The rise in the river ended up washing out the river gauge allowing for only an estimated gauge measurement. These floodwaters continued south along the Pecos River and were recorded at the Lake Arthur gauge.
A strong storm dropped nickel size hail in Las Vegas, NM close to Grande Ave.

Heavy rain resulted in multiple low water crossings along County Road A19A being flooded with several inches of water. Additionally, parts of San Pablo Creek and Tecolote Creek overflowed its banks in the Mineral Hill area.
